notes: The two images show colour-changing glitter statuettes (dolphins, elephant). They are the inspiration for the project, not part of the circuit, so they are not in the graph.
The 3D-printed gnome enclosure (STL files) is not modelled. The manual gives no detail of how the electronics are fixed inside it.
No breadboard is used. All connections are wires soldered to board pads or headers, so each wire end gets a joined edge (method solder) plus an electrical edge.
The wires are modelled as jumper-wire parts. The manual says only 'wires'.
The DS3231 module has a four-pin pass-through on the other side. It is modelled as a new part with duplicate ports (.1 side to the Nano, .2 side to the BME280), each pair conducting.
The Nano Every is powered over USB. The USB cable and power source are not modelled because the manual does not list them as parts.
The manual says the strip uses VDC, DIN and GND. The GND wire was not described explicitly. I assumed it goes to a Nano GND pin (GND.2).
The Nano Every is not in the catalogue, so a new type is created. Its pin names follow the Nano convention, including '3.3V'.
The LED strip DOUT is left unconnected.
The strip is a new type 'ws2812-strip-8' with 8 LEDs, per the sketch NumLEDs=8.
